headline.title: A PHP flaw takes websites offline around the world
headline.quip: Security agencies advised going offline until patched, so part of the web secured itself the old-fashioned way: by not being there.
headline.summary: The PHP team released patches for a critical flaw nicknamed PHP2Shell. CERT-EU, the UK NCSC and the NSA advised taking vulnerable systems offline until patched, and sites including Pinboard, parts of Wikipedia, 4chan and Something Awful went offline. PHP runs about 69% of websites, according to W3Techs.

also.title: Orange’s mobile network fails across France
also.summary: From about 11:20 CEST, Orange and Sosh customers across France lost calls, texts and data, with about 12,000 Downdetector reports. No cause was given.

reasons: Backfilled during setup and reviewed by the owner.
